analysis.title: GS Malmstrom - Few Charts 18 Oct 2026
key_insights: S&P 500 is hovering around all-time highs while the market under the surface is rewarding quality stocks.
The same theme is visible in Europe, where the Quality factor had a few years of underperformance versus the market, ending a long winning streak.
Quality performs well when earnings momentum weakens, which the market is expecting into next year. The Quality premium to the rest of the market is now below its level in recent years.

The AI trade was volatile this week. On Wednesday GS prime brokerage data showed the largest net selling of global AI stocks in the past year, other than July (-2.8 Z score), driven by long and short sales at 3.5 to 1.

Positioning in AI has come down. Net allocation to global AI stocks fell to 26.1% of total single-stock net, versus about 33% in June. The aggregate long/short ratio is 3.27, versus a peak of 4.34 in June.
US equity multiples have declined this year as bond yields have risen, and equities usually struggle when yields rise sharply.
Corporate balance sheets face limited fundamental risk from higher rates because the increase in interest expense has been manageable. S&P 500 interest coverage (ex Financials) is historically high.
The equity market has downgraded its growth outlook, which shows in Cyclicals vs Defensives performance.
High yield credit spreads have widened, especially for AI-related issuers.
GS expects the earnings boost from AI capex to fade going forward.
The S&P 500 ex AI (SPXAII) has outperformed as AI stocks sold off, and the Momentum factor has unwound much of its recent gains.
US Quality has had one of its strongest periods of outperformance and is at 12-month highs. GS ties the move to higher rates being priced in.
earnings_insights: GS notes the market is expecting earnings momentum to weaken into next year, a backdrop in which Quality has historically performed well.
The earnings boost from AI capex is expected to fade going forward (per GS GIR chart).
